proofs.proof_tex:
Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}complete\text{-}randomization}\), \(K\mid N\), \(n=N/K\), every arm has \(n_a=n\), and the assigned counts exhaust the population:
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a=Kn=N,
\qquad n_{\mathrm u}=0.
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}allocation\text{-}space}\) says that \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}\) is exactly the specialization of \(\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) at \(\mathbf n=n\mathbf 1_K\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\). The balanced law and \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) are therefore uniform on the same finite set, so the hypothesis of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\) holds. Substitution of \(n_a=n\) in that lemma gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}n\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\]
Multiplication on the left and right by \(C\) and \(C^{\mathsf T}\), respectively, yields the displayed formula for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\). The scalar formula follows from the same lemma after substituting \(n_a=n\). Finally, each diagonal \(S_{aa}(Y)\) depends only on the empirical marginal \(F_a\), so only off-diagonal cross-arm covariances vary over \(\mathcal S_N(F)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization with \(n_a\geq1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a\geq0\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}\right\}C^{\mathsf T}
\]
and
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
For fixed armwise empirical marginals \(F\), the diagonal terms are constant over \(\mathcal S_N(F)\). Thus all completion dependence is carried by the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances, whose coefficients are independent of \(\mathbf n\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(T_{ia}=\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)\) and \(p_a=n_a/N\). Feasibility of \(\mathbf n\) gives \(n_a\geq1\), \(\sum_a n_a\leq N\), and, because \(K\geq2\), \(N\geq2\). Hence every denominator below is positive. By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}sample\text{-}assign\text{-}randomization}\), \(Z\) is uniform on the support in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}sample\text{-}assign\text{-}design}\). Counting fixed-label allocations gives
\[
\mathbb E_ZT_{ia}=p_a,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ja})=\frac{n_a(n_a-1)}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j),
\tag{1}
\]
and, for \(a\ne b\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ib})=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{jb})=\frac{n_an_b}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j).
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, a fixed position has label \(a\) in the fraction \(n_a/N\) of the support; conditional on that event, \(n_a-1\) of the remaining \(N-1\) positions have label \(a\), and \(n_b\) have label \(b\). The same count remains valid when \(n_{\mathrm u}>0\), because \(a_{\mathrm u}\) is another fixed-count assignment label.

Write \(y_i^a=Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\). By the definitions of \(\bar Y\) and \(S(Y)\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^a=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^N(y_i^a)^2=(N-1)S_{aa}(Y),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^ay_i^b=(N-1)S_{ab}(Y).
\tag{3}
\]
Equation (1) first gives design unbiasedness:
\[
\mathbb E_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
=\frac1{n_a}\sum_{i=1}^Np_aY_i(a)=\bar Y(a).
\tag{4}
\]
For \(i\ne j\), equation (1) yields
\[
\operatorname{Var}_Z(T_{ia})=p_a(1-p_a),
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ja})=-\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{N-1}.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a=-\sum_i(y_i^a)^2\), equations (3)--(5) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
&=\frac1{n_a^2}\left[
p_a(1-p_a)\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
-\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a
\right]\\
&=\frac{p_a(1-p_a)N}{n_a^2(N-1)}\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
=\left(\frac1{n_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{aa}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
For distinct arms, equation (2) gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ib})=-p_ap_b,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{jb})=\frac{p_ap_b}{N-1}\quad(i\ne j).
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b=-\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b\), equations (3), (4), and (7) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\}
&=\frac1{n_an_b}\left[
-p_ap_b\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b
+\frac{p_ap_b}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b
\right]\\
&=-\frac{p_ap_bN}{n_an_b(N-1)}\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b
=-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) proves
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(\widehat\tau=C\widehat{\bar Y}\), covariance equivariance gives the displayed formula for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\). Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}contrast\text{-}risk}\), cyclicity of trace, and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) then yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_W(Y)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[H\left\{
\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N
\right\}\right]\\
&=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal S_N(F)\) fixes the multiset in each arm, hence every \(S_{aa}(Y)\). Equation (10) proves the completion-dependence assertion.

For the smallest exhaustive audit with an unassigned unit, take \(K=2\), \(N=3\), \(n_1=n_2=1\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=1\). The support consists of all six placements of the labels \(1,2,a_{\mathrm u}\). Each selected arm index is uniform on \(\{1,2,3\}\), and the ordered pair of selected indices is uniform over the six distinct pairs. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
=\frac13\sum_i(y_i^a)^2=\frac23S_{aa}(Y)
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(1),\widehat{\bar Y}(2)\mid Y\}
=\frac16\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^1y_j^2
=-\frac16\sum_i y_i^1y_i^2=-\frac13S_{12}(Y),
\]
exactly matching (6) and (8).
added_lemmas.justification: This identity exposes the unequal-count diagonal coefficients and proves that every completion-dependent coefficient is invariant to the sampling fractions and the unassigned remainder.
added_lemmas.gap: It supplies the exact finite sample-and-assign algebra needed to remove unnecessary balance, exhaustion, and divisibility restrictions from the rank-cone and Loewner results.
added_lemmas.consumer: The generalized rank-cone theorem, Loewner boundary, omnibus corollary, and finite two-arm Aronow--Green--Lee specialization use this node.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the finite two-arm sample-and-assign design of Aronow, Green, and Lee, \(N\geq4\), \(n_{\mathrm s}\) units are sampled without replacement, \(m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) sampled units are treated, \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) are controls, and \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\) are unassigned. For the difference-in-means estimator, their Equation (2) is
\[
V_N=\frac1{N-1}\left\{
\frac{N-m_{\mathrm t}}{m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{11}^{(N)}(Y)
+\frac{N-(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t})}{n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{00}^{(N)}(Y)
+2\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)
\right\}.
\]
Given the two finite-population marginal distributions, their Lemma 1 gives sharp lower and upper bounds for \(\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)\), with the upper endpoint attained by the comonotone coupling. This is an oracle finite-population statement about known marginals, distinct from their subsequent asymptotic analysis of estimated bounds.

source.locator: Section 2, Equation (2), and Section 3, Lemma 1, arXiv:1405.6555v1
source.verbatim_statement: The upper bound is attained if y1 and y0 are comonotonic.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(K\geq2\), \(C\mathbf 1_K=0\), and \(W\succeq0\), and put \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\). The following are equivalent. First, for every \(N\geq K\), every feasible \(\mathbf n=(n_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\) with \(n_a\geq1\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\geq0\), and every collection \(F\) of equal-weight empirical armwise marginals,
\[
Y^{\uparrow}(F)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\rho_W(Y)
\]
under \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\). Second, \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). In fact, the equivalence holds for each fixed feasible \((N,\mathbf n)\). When it holds, for every completion \(Y\),
\[
\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{a<b}(-H_{ab})\left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right]\geq0.
\]
If \(H_{ab}>0\) for some pair, take in each of arms \(a,b\) a binary marginal with one value equal to one and \(N-1\) values equal to zero, and take every other arm constant. Aligning the two ones gives the common-rank completion, while placing them on distinct units gives a feasible completion with exact regret \(-2H_{ab}/\{N(N-1)\}<0\). Thus necessity requires neither balance nor any divisibility condition.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The completion-dependent cross-arm coefficient is exactly minus one over N for every feasible positive fixed-count vector, so the balanced and divisibility restrictions in the current statement are unnecessary. The one-success binary witness proves necessity for every N at least K.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix any \(N\geq K\) and any feasible positive count vector \(\mathbf n\), allowing \(n_{\mathrm u}\geq0\), and use the uniform sample-and-assign law \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\). For a nonzero contrast matrix \(C\),
\[
\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\succeq\Sigma_C(Y)
\quad\text{for every }F\text{ and every }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)
\]
if and only if all columns of \(C\) vanish except two columns that are negatives of one another. Equivalently, every nonzero universally Loewner-dominated multi-contrast system is a vector rescaling of one pairwise arm contrast. For every other \(C\), there are a direction \(h\), two binary armwise marginals, and a feasible completion for which common ranking reduces \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y)\); the one-success construction gives a strict difference \(-2v_av_b/\{N(N-1)\}\), where \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\) and \(v_av_b>0\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The scalar directional reduction uses only the generalized rank-cone equivalence; unequal arm counts and optional nonassignment do not alter the subspace classification.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(K=2\), let the present arms \(1,2\) correspond to Aronow--Green--Lee treatment labels \(1,0\), let \(m=1\), \(C=(1,-1)\), and \(W=(1)\). Suppose \(N\geq4\), \(4\leq n_{\mathrm s}\leq N\), and \(2\leq m_{\mathrm t}\leq n_{\mathrm s}-2\), and specialize the fixed counts to
\[
n_1=m_{\mathrm t},\qquad n_2=n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t},\qquad n_{\mathrm u}=N-n_{\mathrm s}.
\]
First drawing a simple random sample of \(n_{\mathrm s}\) units and then choosing uniformly \(m_{\mathrm t}\) treated units inside that sample induces exactly \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\), the uniform law over the three cells of sizes \(m_{\mathrm t}\), \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\), and \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\). With \(S_{ab}(Y)=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}(Y)/(N-1)\), the fixed-count risk identity becomes term by term Aronow, Green, and Lee's Equation (2):
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\frac1{N-1}\left\{
\frac{N-m_{\mathrm t}}{m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{11}^{(N)}(Y)
+\frac{N-(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t})}{n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{00}^{(N)}(Y)
+2\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)
\right\}.
\]
The diagonal terms are fixed by the two marginal schedules, and Aronow, Green, and Lee's Lemma 1 gives the sharp upper covariance endpoint, attained by the comonotone completion \(Y^{\uparrow}(F)\). This is an exact finite oracle recovery for known marginal distributions, not a claim about their subsequent asymptotics for estimated bounds.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current balanced two-arm statement omits the sampled-but-not-exhaustive design analyzed by Aronow, Green, and Lee. The corrected statement identifies the sequential law with the uniform three-cell law and matches their finite oracle variance formula and sharp endpoint.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If the rows of \(C\) form an orthonormal basis of the zero-sum contrast space and \(W=I_{K-1}\), then \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\) and \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\ne b\), so \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). Hence, for every \(N\geq K\), every feasible positive count vector \(\mathbf n\), and every nonnegative unassigned remainder, common ranks maximize the sum of the randomization variances of the complete orthonormal contrast system. When \(K>2\), the generalized Loewner boundary still rules out universal covariance-matrix dominance.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The projector calculation is design-independent and the generalized rank-cone theorem makes the omnibus conclusion valid for every feasible fixed-count sample-and-assign design.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume \(K\mid N\), put \(n=N/K\), and restrict to the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\). Let \(H\in\mathbb S_+^K\) and \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). Put \(J=\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\). For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define the symmetric \(|J|\times|J|\) matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) by
\[
B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}
=\frac{H_{ab}}{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}
\left[(d_r)_i(d_s)_j-(d_r)_{\sigma_a(i)}(d_s)_{\sigma_b(j)}\right].
\]
Then \(\Omega^\pi\in\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) if and only if \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive for every \(\sigma\), meaning \(u^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}u\geq0\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^J\). Consequently,
\[
[\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there exists }\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\text{ such that every }B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
For any real symmetric matrix \(B\) indexed by \(J\), copositivity has the finite support characterization
\[
B\text{ is copositive}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}=\varnothing
\]
for every nonempty \(I\subseteq J\) and every negative real eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) of the principal matrix \(B[I]\).

If, in addition, the entries of \(H\) and \(\Omega\) are supplied as exact real-algebraic numbers, in particular as rational numbers, these equivalences give a finite exact recognition algorithm. It enumerates \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), and nonempty \(I\), isolates every negative algebraic eigenvalue of \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), and decides by exact ordered-field linear feasibility whether its eigenspace meets \(\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\). A noncopositivity certificate consists of \((I,\lambda,v)\) with \(v\in\ker\{B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\); it yields explicit ordered columns with at most \(N\) levels and a strict loss improvement. A certificate that a fixed \(\pi\) works consists of the finite collection of infeasibility certificates for all these negative-eigenspace tests. Thus a yes instance returns such a \(\pi\), while a no instance returns, for every \(\pi\), a corresponding strict cut witness. No algebraic enumeration claim is made for unrestricted real inputs, and the exhaustive algorithm is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Generalizing N globally requires making the theorem's already-intended balanced exhaustive domain explicit. The copositivity characterization and exact-algebraic algorithm are otherwise unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume \(K\mid N\), put \(n=N/K\), and restrict throughout to the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\). Fix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) and a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either by exact entries or by a rational inducing law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). Characterize \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this domain and hence \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): decide whether some \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and rational input bit length that returns a relabelling and finite cut certificate on yes instances, and arm-specific binary ordered columns with a strict exact improvement on no instances; if binary separation is incomplete, characterize the minimal complete finite alphabet. This question does not range over the arbitrary-count uniform sample-and-assign domain.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unresolved polynomial-recognition and minimal-alphabet question remains exactly on the balanced exhaustive kernel domain and must not be conflated with arbitrary-count uniform designs.

proposed_assumptions.condition: The assignment obeys \(Z\sim\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) for the feasible count vector \(\mathbf n\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}sample\text{-}assign\text{-}design}\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This names the known assignment distribution used by the generalized design-based covariance identity; count feasibility and positivity are part of the preceding design definition and symbol domains.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This fixes only the known randomization law. The covariance identity, rank-cone boundary, and optimality claims are derived rather than assumed.

proposed.construction:
For a feasible count vector \(\mathbf n=(n_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\), let \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a\) and
\[
\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}
=\left\{z\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm u}^{N}:
\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n_a\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A,
\quad
\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf 1(z_i=a_{\mathrm u})=n_{\mathrm u}
\right\}.
\]
The uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law is
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}(Z=z)
=\lvert\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\rvert^{-1}
\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\}.
\]
The label \(a_{\mathrm u}\) records an unassigned unit and has no associated observed arm outcome. For each assigned arm,
\[
\widehat{\bar Y}(a)=\frac{1}{n_a}\sum_{i:Z_i=a}Y_i(a).
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This separately defines the broadened uniform design, its optional unassigned cell, and the correctly normalized observed arm means.

proposed.condition: On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), with \(n=N/K\), \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), the assignment \(Z\) is uniform over \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}\).

proposed.name: Balanced exhaustive allocation subdomain
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), put \(n=N/K\), specialize \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), and define
\[
\mathcal Z_{N,K}=\left\{z\in\mathcal A^N:\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}=\mathcal Z_{N,n\mathbf 1_K}^{\mathrm{sa}}\). This is the support used only by the balanced assignment-law and kernel domains.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The legacy allocation space is explicitly the balanced exhaustive specialization of the new support.

proposed.name: Valid balanced assignment laws
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), with \(n=N/K\), \(n_a=n\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), define
\[
\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}=\left\{p\in\Delta(\mathcal Z_{N,K}):\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,K}}p(z)\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=K^{-1}\text{ for every }i\text{ and }a\right\}.
\]
Thus every law has exactly \(n\) assignments to each arm, no unassigned units, total mass one, nonnegative atom probabilities, and \(\Pr_p(Z_i=a)=1/K\), without unit- or arm-exchangeability.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The balanced law class is localized to equal counts and no unassigned remainder.

proposed.name: Admissible balanced covariance tensors
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), with \(n=N/K\), \(n_a=n\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), define
\[
\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}=\left\{\Omega:\exists p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K},\quad \Omega_{abij}=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,K}}p(z)\{K\mathbf 1(z_i=a)-1\}\{K\mathbf 1(z_j=b)-1\}\right\}.
\]
This finite moment-polytope representation is the exact feasibility constraint. Every member satisfies \(\Omega_{abij}=\Omega_{baji}\), \(\sum_a\Omega_{abij}=\sum_b\Omega_{abij}=0\), \(\sum_i\Omega_{abij}=\sum_j\Omega_{abij}=0\), \(\Omega_{aaii}=K-1\), \(\Omega_{abii}=-1\) for \(a\ne b\), \(-1\leq\Omega_{abij}\leq K-1\), and positive semidefiniteness of the \(NK\times NK\) matrix indexed by \((a,i)\). No further permutation symmetry is imposed, and these displayed consequences without the probability-simplex representation are not sufficient for feasibility.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact covariance-moment image remains a balanced exhaustive construction.

proposed.name: Equivalence of balanced kernels under unit relabelling
proposed.construction: On the balanced exhaustive kernel domain \(K\mid N\), for \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\), define \((\Omega^{\pi})_{abij}=\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}\). Write \(\Omega\cong\Omega'\) exactly when \(\Omega'=\Omega^{\pi}\) for some \(\pi\), and set \([\Omega]_{\cong}=\{\Omega^{\pi}:\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orbit relation is explicitly situated on the balanced exhaustive kernel domain.

proposed.name: Balanced-kernel covariance loss
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), with \(n=N/K\), \(n_a=n\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), for \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define
\[
\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\sigma)=\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}\sum_{i,j=1}^N H_{ab}\Omega_{abij}x^a_{\sigma_a(i)}x^b_{\sigma_b(j)}.
\]
If \(\Omega\) is induced by \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), this equals \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_p(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\) for the schedule with arm columns \(x^a\circ\sigma_a\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The N-squared normalization is correct only for the balanced exhaustive coding used by this kernel class.

proposed.name: Universal identity-optimal tensor cone
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive kernel domain \(K\mid N\), define
\[
\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)=\left\{\Omega\in\mathbb R^{K\times K\times N\times N}:\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\sigma)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal M_N^K\text{ and }\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\right\}.
\]
It is a closed convex cone because every defining comparison is homogeneous and linear in \(\Omega\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This cone is explicitly the one induced by the retained balanced-kernel loss.

proposed.name: Admissible rank-preserving kernel classes
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(K\mid N\), with \(n=N/K\), \(n_a=n\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), define
\[
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)=\left\{[\Omega]_{\cong}:\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K},\ [\Omega]_{\cong}\cap\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\neq\varnothing\right\}.
\]
Recognition is posed only for an input tensor already in \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), equivalently with a valid inducing law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). This domain is distinct from arbitrary-count uniform sample-and-assign designs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The recognition domain remains separate from arbitrary-count uniform sample-and-assign laws.

proposed.name: Cut-generator handle for balanced assignment kernels
proposed.construction:
On the balanced exhaustive kernel domain \(K\mid N\), starting from \(x^a\in\mathcal M_N\), use
\[
x^a=x^a_1\mathbf 1_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}(x^a_{r+1}-x^a_r)d_r.
\]
Insert these nonnegative adjacent increments into \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}\), quotient by \([\Omega]_{\cong}\), and seek a finite cut-product separation certificate for membership in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\). This handle does not range over the general sample-and-assign domain.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The computational handle is localized to the same balanced kernel problem as its consumer theorem and OEQ.

proposed.statement:
Under balanced complete randomization,
\[
\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}\right\}C^{\mathsf T}
\]
and hence
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
Therefore all completion dependence is carried by the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances.
proposed.justification: This balanced corollary preserves the exact covariance arithmetic used by the finite audits while making its specialization status explicit.
proposed.gap: The maximal identity is now carried by the arbitrary-count fixed-count lemma, so this node no longer presents the balanced subdomain as the headline.
proposed.consumer: The balanced K equals 3, N equals 6 audits and the balanced-kernel subdomain continue to cite this exact specialization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing balanced claim is unchanged, but its proof basis must be rewired through the new general covariance lemma without self-dependence.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(K\geq2\), \(C\mathbf 1_K=0\), and \(W\succeq0\), and put \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\). The following are equivalent. First, for every \(N\geq K\), every feasible \(\mathbf n=(n_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\) with \(n_a\geq1\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\geq0\), and every collection \(F\) of equal-weight empirical armwise marginals,
\[
Y^{\uparrow}(F)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\rho_W(Y)
\]
under \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\). Second, \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). In fact, the equivalence holds for each fixed feasible \((N,\mathbf n)\). When it holds, for every completion \(Y\),
\[
\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{a<b}(-H_{ab})\left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right]\geq0.
\]
If \(H_{ab}>0\) for some pair, take in each of arms \(a,b\) a binary marginal with one value equal to one and \(N-1\) values equal to zero, and take every other arm constant. Aligning the two ones gives the common-rank completion, while placing them on distinct units gives a feasible completion with exact regret \(-2H_{ab}/\{N(N-1)\}<0\). Thus necessity requires neither balance nor any divisibility condition.
proposed.justification: The theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient, \(\mathcal O(K^2)\) certificate uniform over all positive fixed arm counts and optional unassigned units.
proposed.gap: Existing sharp two-arm work and multi-arm covariance algebra do not identify this count-invariant universal contrast-geometry boundary.
proposed.consumer: A multi-arm causal-bootstrap implementation can replace integer optimization by one common sort exactly when the reported contrast loss lies in the graph-Laplacian cone.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim and dependency graph must move together to the arbitrary-count fixed-count lemma.

proposed.statement:
Fix any \(N\geq K\) and any feasible positive count vector \(\mathbf n\), allowing \(n_{\mathrm u}\geq0\), and use the uniform sample-and-assign law \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\). For a nonzero contrast matrix \(C\),
\[
\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\succeq\Sigma_C(Y)
\quad\text{for every }F\text{ and every }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)
\]
if and only if all columns of \(C\) vanish except two columns that are negatives of one another. Equivalently, every nonzero universally Loewner-dominated multi-contrast system is a vector rescaling of one pairwise arm contrast. For every other \(C\), there are a direction \(h\), two binary armwise marginals, and a feasible completion for which common ranking reduces \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y)\); the one-success construction gives a strict difference \(-2v_av_b/\{N(N-1)\}\), where \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\) and \(v_av_b>0\).
proposed.justification: This theorem gives the exact matrix-dominance boundary uniformly over unequal arm counts and optional unassigned units.
proposed.gap: No located causal-bootstrap or multi-arm design result classifies when one completion dominates the full covariance matrix on this finite sample-and-assign class.
proposed.consumer: Analysts constructing simultaneous Wald regions learn when one rank completion is valid and when contrast-specific completion is unavoidable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Loewner statement inherits the generalized scalar theorem and the count-free binary witness.

proposed.statement:
Let \(K=2\), let the present arms \(1,2\) correspond to Aronow--Green--Lee treatment labels \(1,0\), let \(m=1\), \(C=(1,-1)\), and \(W=(1)\). Suppose \(N\geq4\), \(4\leq n_{\mathrm s}\leq N\), and \(2\leq m_{\mathrm t}\leq n_{\mathrm s}-2\), and specialize the fixed counts to
\[
n_1=m_{\mathrm t},\qquad n_2=n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t},\qquad n_{\mathrm u}=N-n_{\mathrm s}.
\]
First drawing a simple random sample of \(n_{\mathrm s}\) units and then choosing uniformly \(m_{\mathrm t}\) treated units inside that sample induces exactly \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\), the uniform law over the three cells of sizes \(m_{\mathrm t}\), \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\), and \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\). With \(S_{ab}(Y)=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}(Y)/(N-1)\), the fixed-count risk identity becomes term by term Aronow, Green, and Lee's Equation (2):
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\frac1{N-1}\left\{
\frac{N-m_{\mathrm t}}{m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{11}^{(N)}(Y)
+\frac{N-(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t})}{n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{00}^{(N)}(Y)
+2\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)
\right\}.
\]
The diagonal terms are fixed by the two marginal schedules, and Aronow, Green, and Lee's Lemma 1 gives the sharp upper covariance endpoint, attained by the comonotone completion \(Y^{\uparrow}(F)\). This is an exact finite oracle recovery for known marginal distributions, not a claim about their subsequent asymptotics for estimated bounds.
proposed.justification: This is the exact finite sanity check against the canonical two-stage sample-and-assign oracle result, including unsampled units.
proposed.gap: The comparison must recover both the design law and every normalization term, not merely the balanced two-arm ray.
proposed.consumer: Two-arm causal-bootstrap software obtains a verified finite oracle specialization while keeping estimated-bound asymptotics outside scope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proposition is strengthened to the full AGL design and cites Equation (2) and Lemma 1 at their distinct roles.

proposed.statement: If the rows of \(C\) form an orthonormal basis of the zero-sum contrast space and \(W=I_{K-1}\), then \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\) and \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\ne b\), so \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). Hence, for every \(N\geq K\), every feasible positive count vector \(\mathbf n\), and every nonnegative unassigned remainder, common ranks maximize the sum of the randomization variances of the complete orthonormal contrast system. When \(K>2\), the generalized Loewner boundary still rules out universal covariance-matrix dominance.
proposed.justification: This nondegenerate multi-arm case separates a valid count-uniform omnibus scalarization from invalid joint covariance dominance.
proposed.gap: Complete contrast systems are standard, but their sharp common-rank endpoint has not been stated uniformly over arbitrary fixed arm counts.
proposed.consumer: Factorial and analysis-of-variance designs obtain an analytic least-favourable total-variance benchmark under unequal allocation and optional nonassignment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The omnibus corollary is generalized with its parent theorems.

proposed.statement:
Assume \(K\mid N\), put \(n=N/K\), and restrict to the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\). Let \(H\in\mathbb S_+^K\) and \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). Put \(J=\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\). For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define the symmetric \(|J|\times|J|\) matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) by
\[
B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}
=\frac{H_{ab}}{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}
\left[(d_r)_i(d_s)_j-(d_r)_{\sigma_a(i)}(d_s)_{\sigma_b(j)}\right].
\]
Then \(\Omega^\pi\in\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) if and only if \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive for every \(\sigma\), meaning \(u^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}u\geq0\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^J\). Consequently,
\[
[\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there exists }\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\text{ such that every }B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
For any real symmetric matrix \(B\) indexed by \(J\), copositivity has the finite support characterization
\[
B\text{ is copositive}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}=\varnothing
\]
for every nonempty \(I\subseteq J\) and every negative real eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) of the principal matrix \(B[I]\).

If, in addition, the entries of \(H\) and \(\Omega\) are supplied as exact real-algebraic numbers, in particular as rational numbers, these equivalences give a finite exact recognition algorithm. It enumerates \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), and nonempty \(I\), isolates every negative algebraic eigenvalue of \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), and decides by exact ordered-field linear feasibility whether its eigenspace meets \(\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\). A noncopositivity certificate consists of \((I,\lambda,v)\) with \(v\in\ker\{B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\); it yields explicit ordered columns with at most \(N\) levels and a strict loss improvement. A certificate that a fixed \(\pi\) works consists of the finite collection of infeasibility certificates for all these negative-eigenspace tests. Thus a yes instance returns such a \(\pi\), while a no instance returns, for every \(\pi\), a corresponding strict cut witness. No algebraic enumeration claim is made for unrestricted real inputs, and the exhaustive algorithm is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
proposed.justification: The theorem remains the computable exact characterization of the nonexchangeable balanced exhaustive subdomain.
proposed.gap: Its exhaustive algorithm does not establish polynomial complexity, and its multilevel witnesses do not settle binary completeness.
proposed.consumer: Small balanced designs with exact algebraic kernels can be audited without suggesting that the result covers arbitrary-count kernels.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Only the previously implicit K-divides-N, equal-count, zero-remainder domain is surfaced; the mathematical characterization is preserved.

proposed.statement: Assume \(K\mid N\), put \(n=N/K\), and restrict throughout to the balanced exhaustive subdomain \(n_a=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\). Fix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) and a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either by exact entries or by a rational inducing law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). Characterize \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this domain and hence \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): decide whether some \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and rational input bit length that returns a relabelling and finite cut certificate on yes instances, and arm-specific binary ordered columns with a strict exact improvement on no instances; if binary separation is incomplete, characterize the minimal complete finite alphabet. This question does not range over the arbitrary-count uniform sample-and-assign domain.
proposed.justification: The residual computational question remains on the realizable nonexchangeable balanced exhaustive moment polytope.
proposed.gap: Polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with binary completeness or a minimal-alphabet characterization, remains open.
proposed.consumer: A solution would turn the exact but exhaustive balanced-kernel audit into a scalable certificate with standardized witnesses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The OEQ is explicitly prevented from drifting into the newly generalized uniform design domain.

proposed.citation: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee (2014). Sharp bounds on the variance in randomized experiments. The Annals of Statistics 42(3), 850--871. arXiv:1405.6555v1. doi:10.1214/13-AOS1200.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The versioned arXiv handle records the exact source inspected for Equation (2) and Lemma 1.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: For every feasible positive fixed-count sample-and-assign design, including an optional unassigned remainder, \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C^{\mathsf T}WC\in\mathcal R_K.\]
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must name the generalized design class and no longer imply balanced exhaustive assignment.

proposed.comparator_claim: Equation (2) gives the exact finite-population difference-in-means variance with treated, control, and unsampled counts, and Lemma 1 gives the sharp comonotone covariance endpoint from known marginals.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Comparator positioning is synchronized to the full finite AGL oracle recovery and the new fixed-count covariance lemma.

prose_updates.tldr: Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization with arbitrary positive arm counts and any nonnegative unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) exactly when \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. The off-diagonal completion objective and exact \(2/N\) regret identity do not depend on the arm counts. The result includes the full finite two-arm Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design, while balanced complete randomization remains an exact subdomain for the six-unit audits and the separate balanced-kernel copositivity theory. For admissible balanced covariance tensors, finite exact recognition remains available for exact real-algebraic inputs; polynomial-time recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee give the sharp two-arm oracle endpoint for a random sample assigned with fixed treated and control counts, while generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact multi-arm contrast-geometry boundary that is uniform over unequal positive arm counts and optional unsampled units. On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design, a sharper classification for joint covariance dominance, and, on the distinct balanced nonexchangeable domain, an exact cut-copositivity representation modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the unequal-count sample-and-assign covariance decomposition, proves that its completion-dependent term is count-free, and uses finite rearrangement plus isolated binary witnesses to obtain the graph-Laplacian equivalence, exact regret, and Loewner classification without balance or divisibility restrictions. It recovers the full finite Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design with the normalization \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), retains exact balanced six-unit audits, and keeps the general balanced-kernel copositivity theorem and its computational residual questions on their original subdomain.

sampling_model.design: The headline design is uniform over assignments with prespecified positive arm counts \(n_a\geq1\) and an optional unassigned count \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\geq0\). Balanced complete randomization, with \(K\mid N\), \(n_a=N/K\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), is retained as an exact subdomain. The separate kernel problem continues to range only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), so the general uniform-design and balanced-kernel domains are not conflated.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling. An unassigned label records units omitted from the experimental sample without making the potential outcomes random.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object. Under the headline law it uniformly chooses disjoint arm samples of sizes \(n_a\), leaving \(n_{\mathrm u}\) units unassigned; under the separate nonexchangeable balanced analysis it follows the known admissible law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every reported arm has known positive probability \(n_a/N>0\). The unassigned probability \(n_{\mathrm u}/N\) may be zero, and no outcome mean is defined for the unassigned label.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural endpoint conditions on the full armwise empirical marginals \(F\) and is therefore an oracle finite-population completion result. Aronow, Green, and Lee's Equation (2) and Lemma 1 supply the exact two-arm oracle benchmark; their asymptotic analysis of bounds estimated from observed marginal samples is not claimed here.

prose_updates.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee study \(N\geq4\) fixed units, sample \(n_{\mathrm s}\) without replacement, assign \(m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) to treatment and \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) to control, and leave \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\) unsampled. Their Equation (2) is exactly the two-arm specialization of the fixed-count covariance identity after \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), and their Lemma 1 supplies the sharp comonotone oracle endpoint. This finite known-marginal equivalence is distinct from their subsequent asymptotic theory for estimated bounds. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion for a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance algebra but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem agrees with the pairwise rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here is finite and direct. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The separate general-kernel theorem remains restricted to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a finite cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result is a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem, not the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
prose_updates.interpretation: For any uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner can ignore the unequal diagonal sampling coefficients when comparing potential-outcome completions: only the common term \(-N^{-1}\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}\) varies. Nonpositive off-diagonal entries of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\) certify one-sort least-favourable completion, while a positive entry identifies two arms on which a finite binary reversal strictly improves the loss. This conclusion and the \(2/N\) regret identity are unchanged by unequal allocation or unsampled units. Matrix-valued conservativeness remains much rarer, and the nonexchangeable balanced-design analogue remains a finite copositivity problem rather than part of the generalized uniform design.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate is an oracle completion theorem for a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not estimate unknown armwise marginals and does not turn the endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. The full Aronow--Green--Lee finite design and sharp known-marginal endpoint are recovered, but their estimated-bound asymptotics are not reproved. For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the copositivity theorem is exhaustive rather than scalable: it enumerates factorially many relabellings and arm permutations and exponentially many supports, and strict witnesses may use as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The uniform fixed-count cone theorem follows from exact assignment-indicator moments, the count-free cross-arm covariance coefficient, a finite rearrangement proof, and a contrast-geometry necessity construction. Its domain permits arbitrary positive arm counts and a nonnegative unassigned remainder; balanced complete randomization is only a retained specialization. The two-arm statement recovers the Aronow--Green--Lee oracle variance formula and sharp comonotone endpoint, not their asymptotic estimated-bound results.
